messages:
alice: Handoff — quick summary before I go. Embeddings service started degrading at ~01:12 UTC. p50 stable, but p95/p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~350-420ms. Error rate for embed-worker requests up to 2.3% (timeouts + 502s). Low-priority customers are already on quantized-cpu fallback.

alice: Current mitigations in flight: applied temporary circuit-breaker on heavy_batch route, scaled embed-worker to +2 replicas, and triggered a rolling restart of embed-worker-3 (pod was reporting OOM-adj spikes). Watching metrics.

ben: Can you paste the last 20 lines from embed-worker-3 logs? want to see OOM vs GC.

alice: pasted log excerpt below:
```
2026-03-17T01:11:58Z embed-worker-3 INFO kvcache: miss for key batch-9
2026-03-17T01:12:03Z embed-worker-3 WARN mem: high-alloc 89% (limit 96%)
2026-03-17T01:12:12Z embed-worker-3 ERROR inference: model step timeout 120s
2026-03-17T01:12:12Z embed-worker-3 ERROR http: 502 from runtime
2026-03-17T01:12:25Z embed-worker-3 INFO lifecycle: restarting container
```

alice: Looks like model step timeouts coinciding with mem pressure. Not a pure network blip.

charlie: Re: config — did the quantized model rollout happen recently? I remember we pushed a small change to cpu-fallback routing yesterday. Could that change increase mem churn?

alice: We rolled the routing change 2026-03-16T22:45 UTC (small traffic-split tweak). No model binary changes. But routing could shift batch sizes onto certain workers.

charlie: I'll investigate batching distribution and bucket math. If a few workers got large batches, KV cache pressure can spike.

oncall-bot: [automated] deploy/quantized-fallback routing-change completed at 2026-03-16T22:45:12Z; rollout=100%, owner=charlie.

ben: For handoff to dana: next steps I recommend — 1) keep the circuit-breaker on heavy_batch, 2) hold any non-urgent deploys to embed infra, 3) if embed-worker-3 restarts do not escalate immediately unless errors persist >10m, 4) I opened a short-lived canary to route 10% of heavy load to embed-canary-2.

dana: I'll take over at 02:00 UTC. Action items for me: check the canary health, look at batch-size distribution across workers, and coordinate a quick rollback of the routing change if evidence looks strong. I'll also notify product if we need a temporary customer-facing msg.

alice: FYI I've pinned the oncall playbook section: /runbooks/embeddings-degradation and left a note under incident ticket #INC-2871 with the mem traces.

dana: thumbs, taking it. If I see repeat timeouts after restart, I'll trigger an emergency revert and open a postmortem.

charlie: I'll add a quick check to our autoscaler config to avoid >32 item batches routing to a single worker; pushing a patch to a testing branch now.

ben: Also, CPU/IO on the NVMe host looked fine earlier, so likely in-process memory fragmentation. If reverting routing doesn't help, consider temp-lowering max_batch_size to 16 for 30m window.

alice: Leaving these notes and logs in the thread. I'll be offline in ~5m. Thanks — :wave:

dana: Thanks alice. I'll post an update by 02:15 UTC after the canary health check. :thumbsup:
